claims.text: Superconducting behavior in high-entropy superconducting alloys is governed primarily by electron–phonon coupling modulated by local chemical disorder.
Increased electronic scattering alone is not the primary governor of superconducting behavior in these alloys.
Subtle off-stoichiometric variations can increase local chemical disorder.
Enhanced local chemical disorder weakens the electron–phonon interaction.
A reduction in effective electron–phonon coupling weakens Cooper pairing and lowers the superconducting transition temperature.
The proposed equiatomic (TaNb)(ZrHfTi) baseline is a single-phase disordered solid solution.
The proposed baseline exhibits established BCS-like superconductivity.
Local atomic disorder alters lattice vibrational modes and thus the local electron–phonon-coupling landscape.
Local atomic disorder alters the electronic density of states and local electronic structure.
Off-stoichiometric modification can vary local disorder while leaving the overall electron count nearly constant.
The modified alloys will remain disordered and BCS-like superconductors despite the proposed weakening of electron–phonon coupling.
Off-stoichiometric alloys with enhanced local disorder will have a lower Tc than the equiatomic baseline.
Off-stoichiometric alloys with enhanced local disorder will have a lower electron–phonon coupling constant than the baseline.
A smaller specific-heat jump at Tc and altered superconducting-gap measurements would evidence reduced electron–phonon coupling.
The proposed mechanism applies only within a single-phase disordered regime and when electron count is not significantly changed.
Phase separation or large changes in electron concentration would place the alloy outside the mechanism's boundary conditions.
The quantitative relationship among disorder, electron–phonon coupling, and Tc is not established and may be confounded by electron-count changes or impurity phases.
The specific-heat jump at Tc can be used directly to extract the electron–phonon coupling constant.
